newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran exerting pressure, missing editor's wife says.
newsitem.headline: Iran exerting pressure, missing editor's wife says.

text.p: The wife of an arrested Iranian journalist whose fate is causing concern in Bonn said on Tuesday Tehran was putting pressure on her to disown a letter he wrote describing how Iran tried to make him confess to spying.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has written two letters to Iran concerning Faraj Sarkuhi, whose wife and children live in Germany. Tehran says it arrested Sarkuhi for trying to leave Iran illegally earlier this month.

Sarkuhi's wife Farideh Zebarjad told German radio Deutsche Welle that Sarkuhi's brother, himself in prison, had contacted her to say that if she cooperated with Tehran, her husband could be released in two or three months.
She said Sarkuhi's brother appeared to be acting under pressure from the Iranian authorities.
He urged her to dismiss as a forgery a letter from Sarkuhi which Bonn believes is genuine, and which was published in several Western European newspapers last month.
The letter alleges Sarkuhi was held and tortured by the Iranian secret service in Tehran late last year to force him to confess to spying for Germany.

Iran insists he was in Germany at the time, but the letter says Iran sent someone to Germany with Sarkuhi's passport to secure an entry stamp. It also says Sarkuhi, editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday), was forced to hold a subsequent news conference insisting he really had flown to Germany.

Zebarjad repeated an allegation that Iran was holding her husband as a bargaining chip to put pressure on German authorities not to convict an Iranian and four Lebanese on trial in Berlin for a 1992 assassination of Kurdish dissidents.

State prosecutors have angered Tehran by accusing the Iranian government of ordering the killings. The trial is expected to end within the next few months. Iran denies any involvement in the killings.
